I've drafted answers for the security/compliance section and attached supporting artifacts. High-level notes:

- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (security) as of 2025-11. Summary attached: SOC2-Summary-2025.pdf. Full report can be delivered under NDA.

- Data residency: Hosted regions available in us-east-1, eu-west-1; private deployment supports full on-prem or customer VPC.
- Pen tests & bug bounty: yearly third-party penetration test (summary available) and HackerOne program for external reports.

Attachments included: Marketplace_Security_Attestation.pdf (summary attestation), SOC2-Summary-2025.pdf

Suggested language for questionnaire: "Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (security) compliant. Redwood does not process or store cardholder data for marketplace billing; marketplace providers handle billing metering and invoicing. For private deployments, customers manage PCI scope."

I'll also redact the SOC2 report and prep a short artifact bundle for Acme. If legal wants specific wording about indemnities or sub-processors, flag and we'll coordinate.

Sarah / Acme team — thanks for the questions. Answers and artifacts below; attaching a marketplace-focused terms exhibit and our standard file set for procurement.

1) PCI / tokenization: Redwood does not store, process, or transmit cardholder data for any marketplace billing flows. We do not retain tokens or cardholder references for marketplace metering. For customer integrations that use third-party payment processors, any tokenization is managed by that processor; Redwood connectors do not persist cardholder tokens. Suggested RFP language you can copy: "Redwood Inference does not process or store cardholder data for marketplace billing. Marketplace providers (AWS/Azure/GCP) are the billing and payment processors for purchases made via their marketplaces."

2) SLA / credits: We maintain an SLA for Dedicated and Hosted customers. For marketplace purchases, the marketplace routing typically enforces provider-level entitlements; our marketplace exhibit (attached) provides the marketplace-friendly SLA appendix (example credit calculation: 5% service credit for monthly uptime < 99.9% and >= 99.0%; 10% credit for monthly uptime < 99.0%). This is illustrative and negotiable per procurement. Attachment: Redwood_Marketplace_Terms_v2.docx

3) Billing entity and consolidated billing:
- AWS Marketplace: Redwood Inference, Inc. (DBA Redwood Inference) appears as vendor; billing and invoicing handled through AWS Marketplace Billing. We support consolidated billing via AWS Organizations and entitlements are tied to customer account IDs.
- Azure Marketplace: Redwood Inference, Inc. — supports marketplace purchase flows via Azure Marketplace; billing goes through Microsoft.
- GCP Marketplace: Redwood Inference, Inc. — billing through GCP Marketplace.

Note: For Enterprise Private deployments purchased off-marketplace, invoices are issued directly by Redwood Inference, Inc. to the customer billing contact.

Attachments: Marketplace_Security_Attestation.pdf, SOC2-Summary-2025.pdf, Redwood_Marketplace_Terms_v2.docx
